title: zane prompt + quant quicklog
content:
Quick morning scratchpad for the prompt/quant experiments I'm juggling. Mainly brain-dumps + runnable snippets so I don't forget steps between meetings. NOT polished.

03/16 AM: Goals for the day
- sanity-check 4-bit quantized llama2-7b for chat prompts used in search-rewrite flow
- validate prefix-KV caching gains for short queries (<= 40 tokens)
- iterate on prompt variants that reduce hallucination on product-spec Qs

Experiment 1: 4-bit qkv + llama2-7b (quantize-aware packing)
- variant A: nf4 + per-channel symmetric, baseline = fp16
- variant B: int4 + per-tensor scales, aggressive smoothing
Run: script: ./tools/quantize_and_run.sh --model llama2-7b --backend triton --quant nf4 --batch 1 --seq 256
Notes:
- first pass: A crashes at step 3 with cuda OOM on 40GB A100 (unexpected) — probably kernel memory fragmentation. Workaround: set TRITON_MAX_SEQ=192 and enable contiguous-weights flag.
- after workaround: variant A stable; latency 58ms/token for first token, 9ms/token steady-state (batch=1)
- model-size reported ~13.8GB resident after quant (vs 27.6GB fp16)
- quality: on small spec-Q dataset (20 queries) A produced 12/20 acceptable answers, B produced 9/20. Baseline fp16 produced 14/20. Need larger eval.

Experiment 2: KV cache prefix hits microbench - setup: synthetic workload of 1000 requests, 80% share a common 16-token prefix, rest random
- metric: median p95 latency, token throughput, cost estimate
- quick results (local sim): with prefix-KV hit enabled: median latency down 37%, p95 down 24%, tokens/sec up 1.8x.
- note: caching helper currently uses LRU eviction that evicts on token-count not on request-frequency; consider moving to frequency-weighted TTL.

Prompt bank (wip)
- base: "You are a product-spec assistant. Given the following product description, produce a short, factual summary and call out ambiguities."
- variants to test:
  * short-instructions: add "Limit output to 3 bullets, each <= 16 words."
  * chain-of-critique: add second-turn prompt: "Now critique the summary for any missing assumption."
  * conservative-mode: prefix with "Respond only if you are >90% confident; otherwise reply 'INSUFFICIENT'"

Quick eval plan (small-scale)
- assemble 200 spec-Qs from GH issues + release notes (seeded)
- run candidates: fp16 baseline, nf4 A, int4 B
- metrics: exact-match on key facts (manual labels for 50), hallucination score (manual), LM-judged helpfulness (pairwise)
- timeline: run overnight on dedicated-node-2 (reserve slot 03/18 02:00-06:00)

Notes on failure modes seen so far
- hallucinations often appear when prompt length > 180 tokens and the model is in aggressive truncation mode: likely due to incomplete context + quant noise. Try conservative-mode prompt and longer KV retention.
- rare repetition loop at token 120-140 with int4 B; might be attention instability — try smoothing scale or disable cross-attn optimizations for int4 path.

Runnable snippets (copied for later)
- quick evaluation command:
  curl -X POST \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data '{"model":"llama2-7b-nf4","input":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":256}' \
    https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate

- local quant command (internal tool): 
  python -m rdw.quant.run --model-path models/llama2-7b --out models/llama2-7b-nf4 --algo nf4 --per-channel

Open questions / to-do (prioritized)
1) Replicate quality eval at scale (200 queries) and generate confusion matrix for which facts fail. Assign to Mikaela for labeling (asked in Slack).
2) Investigate OOM on initial nf4 pass — get SRE to check kernel memory settings on dedicated-node-4. (Ticket created JIRA-AML-4592).
3) Prototype freq-weighted TTL policy for KV cache; quick sim + POC in rust lib. (low effort, high upside)
4) Add an automatic guard in prompt wrapper that switches to conservative-mode when input token count > 180

Personal notes (log)
- 03/16 09:10: meeting with product; they want a 'safe-summary' endpoint by EOW. Rough timeline: small pilot -> 2-week rollout -> integration with search.
- 03/16 11:30: paired with Arjun on eval harness; need to merge GH-PR-511 before running overnight.
- 03/17 15:00: demo to SRE scheduled; show memory/residency improvements and KV hit graphs.

End-of-day quick wins:
- pushed small script to parse p95 across runs (tools/parse_latencies.py)
- left comments on PR for int4 smoothing hyperparam defaults

Misc scratch reminders (one-liners):
- flag to toggle 'conservative-mode' in SDK: rdw.client.Options.conservative = True
- confirm whether dedicated nodes run triton 2.4 or 2.5 (affects kernels)
- remind: back up the 20 query manual labels to confluence page after labeling

——
If I don't open this tomorrow, follow the todo list order: scale eval -> fix OOM -> KV-ttl PoC -> prompt guard.
